summary: This bill bars institutions of higher education from receiving any Department of Homeland Security funds if they have a contract, agreement, donation, or gift from a Confucius Institute, Thousand Talents Program, or Chinese entity of concern, unless the institution ends the relationship or the Secretary grants a one-year national security waiver after consulting the Director of National Intelligence.

scores.thoughts: The bill conditions DHS funding eligibility on universities terminating relationships with Confucius Institutes or certain Chinese entities. It does not increase or decrease overall government spending levels or appropriations; it merely restricts recipients of existing funds. No direct engagement with expanding or reducing spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, coverage, or funding.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No provisions address immigration pathways, borders, or enforcement.
No provisions address abortion access or restrictions.
The bill references Chinese military-civil fusion entities but does not alter U.S. military or defense spending levels.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or protections.
No provisions address welfare programs or social safety net funding.

The bill restricts DHS funding to higher education institutions based on foreign ties. While it affects universities, it does not engage with public school investment, federal education policy, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill targets academic and research relationships with Chinese entities but does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or trade policy.
No provisions address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No provisions address foreign aid funding or policy.
The bill references Chinese entities interfering in elections as a criterion but does not alter voting access or election procedures.
The bill mentions safeguards for sensitive research data but does not regulate technology companies or privacy standards.
No provisions address labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
